new.n: Gold in the pipes: J. F. Ruggles's hidden $20 pieces, Ruggles Block, Bronson
new.pl: Ruggles Block, Bronson village: sold to the post office in 1915; the 1916 Sanborn shows the Post Office in the brick row at the SW corner of Chicago and Matteson streets
new.v: $20 gold pieces packed in plugged iron pipes (several caches; no total given)
new.st: James Francis Ruggles, a Bronson rare-book dealer who died in 1911, distrusted banks after a farmhouse fire melted about $1,200 in gold. He packed $20 gold pieces into plugged iron pipes and hid several in the Ruggles Block, a building of two storeys outside and six half-floors inside, with secret panels. His brothers searched it short of tearing it down, and his brother Lon searched for months after a medium's vision; nothing was found. The block was sold to the post office in 1915. Pin is the 1916 post office corner, not a spot.
new.t: No find reported through 1915. If the 1916 post office building is the Ruggles Block, any pipes left would be in its walls and floors. Private downtown building: look only, permission needed.
src: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Bronson, Sep 1916, sheet 3 (LoC sanborn03935_005)
pinev: 1916 Sanborn sheet 3: Post Office in the two-storey brick row at the SW corner of Chicago and Matteson; that the 1915 post-office building is the Ruggles Block is inferred from the papers, not shown on the map. Corner read from Michigan 1 m lidar street grid (2017); r150 also covers the next corner west.
new.tovw: Lead grade C (treasure thread): three 1915 papers; never found; block fixed only via the 1916 post office
